chunks: “The diyah is complete, and the man is not killed.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: There is no contradiction between the two reports, because the first report only negated that any retaliation (qawad) be upon them both, and it did not negate that diyah be upon them both. The suspicion is only removed by each one of them swearing that he did not intend to kill his companion; then the diyah becomes binding upon him.

key_terms.التُّهْمَةُ: legal suspicion or accusation requiring clarification
key_terms.اَلدِّيَةُ: financial compensation due for wrongful killing
key_terms.يُقْتَلُ: is put to death in legal retaliation

ai.seo_question: When is diyah required even though qisas or retaliation is not carried out?
ai.summary: This passage discusses a legal ruling concerning liability when killing is not treated as intentional homicide requiring retaliation. It explains that there is no contradiction between the reports: retaliation is negated, but the full diyah still remains obligatory after an oath removes the presumption of intentional killing.
